records.name: Arorha
records.held_by: Arorha village elders, answering to the Aroxhu council
records.summary: Arorha is a clay-mound village on the southern shore of Hatandros Bight, the confederacy's sea door. Its people ship Okuwun-Rahei clay and dye north to Thorn and south to Archon, and take tolls from boats that land.

notes.text: Arorha is the north-eastern outlier of the Aroxhu clay-mound country, a village on the first raised ground south of Hatandros Bight where the road from Inoja meets the sea. It exists to move the confederacy's clay, dye and pottery onto coastal boats.

The mounds were raised by the village's founders, a generation or two after the Knahaten Flu (2E 560-603) emptied the coast of Cantemiric Velothi, over ground the Velothi had left fallow. Until the secession East Empire Company boatmen called here for clay; in 4E 201 the landing is the same and the buyers are Argonian.

sources.title: Knahaten Flu emptied the coast; East Empire Company left at the secession; Aroxhu clay-mound confederacy holds Okuwun-Rahei (state 10.1, 10.2)

notes.text: A working village with a short stone-free quay of piled mud-brick and wattle where flat boats unload. Elders from Arorha sit on the Aroxhu council. The warden post at Marshgate Watch to the north takes a toll on goods bound for Thorn, and Arorha pays it.

About eleven Argonians of the Oxhu-Teeleel, mostly clay-diggers, potters and boatmen. The elder is a pot-painter who knows every kiln and every flat boat by its maker. Two or three Dunmer traders from Thorn lodge here while they buy.

sources.title: Knahaten Flu emptied the coast; East Empire Company left at the secession; Aroxhu clay-mound confederacy holds Okuwun-Rahei (state 10.1, 10.2)

notes.text: Red clay, ochre and fired pots go out by boat; salt, dried fish and Thorn's saltrice come back. The tolls Arorha charges outsiders landing on its quay pay for the mound walls. Unfired clay is cheap here, finished glazed ware costs three times as much at Thorn.
The village's hatching-tree is at Aroxhu, three days' walk inland and its eggs go there. A small clay shrine on the quay holds votive pots to the dead; broken ones are left on the shore.

sources.title: Knahaten Flu emptied the coast; East Empire Company left at the secession; Aroxhu clay-mound confederacy holds Okuwun-Rahei (state 10.1, 10.2)

notes.text: A ring of low red mounds, each carrying two or three reed-thatched houses on stilts, stained rust-brown by the clay. Kilns smoke at the water's edge and the shore is crazed red mud. Gulls and swamp-herons crowd the quay at dawn.
Inside the village it is calm. On the shore road to the north, mudcrab swarms and giant snakes are the daily trouble and outlaws from Skeith Isle sometimes land in the dark to take boats.

The elder wants a lost kiln-load of ochre found: the boat that carried it was taken by Skeith smugglers. A broken Velothi ancestor-tablet from Virtluush has turned up in the clay-pits and an old Dunmer trader will pay to know where it came from.

records.name: Bala Karag
records.held_by: No one; ancestor ghosts and sea-birds
records.summary: Bala Karag is a ruined Cantemiric Velothi stronghold on a small rocky island a day's walk from Thorn. The Knahaten Flu emptied it and its lower halls are flooded.

notes.text: A ruined Velothi hold on the rock off the Thorn coast, the nearest of the Hatandros Bight ruins to the city.

Cantemiric Velothi, Dunmer dissidents who settled the eastern seaboard, held this coast until the Knahaten Flu (2E 560-603) killed them all. The hold has stood empty since. Chimeri myth says Mephala led a third of the Velothi into Black Marsh.

sources.title: Knahaten Flu 2E 560-603 ended every Velothi hold; Dunmer relic-buyers at Thorn (state 10.1, 10.3)

notes.text: Empty except for the dead. Thorn's slavers, until the Red Year and later the Warden Marches' toll men both kept away from it. The coast Argonians call it sick ground. The lowest hall stands knee-deep in still black water.

sources.title: Knahaten Flu 2E 560-603 ended every Velothi hold; Dunmer relic-buyers at Thorn (state 10.1, 10.3)

notes.text: No living inhabitants. Ancestor ghosts of the Velothi walk the halls, for the Velothi buried their dead beneath their houses and the flu killed whole families at once.
Once a fortified holding that took tolls from coastal boats. Now it draws scavengers: Velothi bronze, ash-glass and carved ancestor tablets sell at Thorn to Dunmer buyers.

sources.title: Knahaten Flu 2E 560-603 ended every Velothi hold; Dunmer relic-buyers at Thorn (state 10.1, 10.3)

notes.text: The Velothi who came south followed the Mephala-led exile and kept ancestor veneration. Tablets and altar niches remain in the upper halls; the Argonians who pass by say the place is sick and do not leave offerings.
Grey basalt and black volcanic stone in heavy, battered Velothi courses, crusted with barnacles and salt at the base. A broken tower stands on the rock at the end of a causeway of piled stone.

sources.title: Knahaten Flu 2E 560-603 ended every Velothi hold; Dunmer relic-buyers at Thorn (state 10.1, 10.3)

notes.text: Ghosts and skeletons in the halls, cliff-nesting hackwings outside and a water-filled lowest hall where slaughterfish have been trapped.

sources.title: Knahaten Flu 2E 560-603 ended every Velothi hold; Dunmer relic-buyers at Thorn (state 10.1, 10.3)

notes.text: A Dunmer relic-seller in Thorn will pay for the ancestor tablet carved with the family sign of the holding's last lord. The door to the lowest hall is barred from within, and the lord's ghost carries the key.

records.name: Kornakim
records.held_by: No one; ancestor ghosts
records.summary: Kornakim is a ruined Cantemiric Velothi watch-hold on a sandy headland halfway down Hatandros Bight. It was abandoned after the Knahaten Flu and sits above the surf, shunned.

notes.text: A ruined Velothi coastal hold on the headland at the bight's seaward edge, one of the Cantemiric Velothi holds of this coast.
Cantemiric Velothi built along the eastern seaboard between Archon and Thorn and died in the Knahaten Flu (2E 560-603). Its seaward point would suit a watch-hold over the sea lanes.

notes.text: Roofless but standing. A smuggler's lantern sometimes burns on the headland, though the smugglers do not go inside.
The ruin has no residents. It is known to the Skeith smugglers as a landmark and to the Arorha clay-men as a place not to dig.
Once a watch-hold that signalled the Velothi's boats. Now a landmark for smugglers and a source of ash-glass shards that lie on the beach below.

sources.title: Velothi holds along the seaboard died in the Flu 2E 560-603; Skeith smugglers use the headland (state 10.1, 10.2)

notes.text: Velothi ancestor shrine niches line the inner hall. The ghosts of the hold's household remain at their posts.
Dark Velothi stonework in low rounded courses with a broken watch-tower at the seaward end, sand heaped in the courtyard, sea-grass growing through the floor, surf loud against the headland.

sources.title: Velothi holds along the seaboard died in the Flu 2E 560-603; Skeith smugglers use the headland (state 10.1, 10.2)

records.name: Coldbrine Mine
records.held_by: Thorn's field-owners, with a toll to Fort Thornmoth
records.summary: Coldbrine Mine is a rock-salt working in a low bluff south-west of Thorn, worked for Thorn's field-owners under the toll of Fort Thornmoth. Its salt cures the saltrice and fish that Thorn exports.

notes.text: A small rock-salt mine in the rise between Thorn and the bight, worked by hired hands for Thorn's field-owners. The name is the Warden Marches' plain Imperial-style naming for a cold brine pit.

sources.title: East Empire Company labour left at the secession; Warden Marches families keep the Thornmoth country; Thorn exports saltrice and cured fish (state 10.1, 10.2, 10.3)

notes.text: Imperial-era bonded labour first cut the salt-bed for the East Empire Company's saltrice and fish trade; the shafts were kept running by Thorn's field-owners after the Company left.
A handful of workers cut brine-hard salt blocks in two shafts and load them on carts. A warden from Fort Thornmoth comes each month for the toll on the carts.

sources.title: East Empire Company labour left at the secession; Warden Marches families keep the Thornmoth country; Thorn exports saltrice and cured fish (state 10.1, 10.2, 10.3)

notes.text: About five Argonians, descendants of freed labourers, plus an overseer from an old Archein family who keeps the mine's keys and the one cart-horse.

sources.title: East Empire Company labour left at the secession; Warden Marches families keep the Thornmoth country; Thorn exports saltrice and cured fish (state 10.1, 10.2, 10.3)

notes.text: Rock-salt for curing: blocks go to Thorn, ground salt to Arorha for fish. The salt is cheap but its trade is steady.

sources.title: East Empire Company labour left at the secession; Warden Marches families keep the Thornmoth country; Thorn exports saltrice and cured fish (state 10.1, 10.2, 10.3)

notes.text: The workers carry small hatching-stones from their home villages and leave a pinch of salt at the mine mouth for those buried underground.
A cut face of grey-white rock streaked with rust, a timber headframe, wooden carts and stacked salt blocks under reed roofs. The air smells of brine and wet stone.
The older shaft is half-fallen, its side galleries blocked by rock; brine pools with rotting water lie below, and mudcrabs nest in the spoil heap.

records.name: Marshgate Watch
records.held_by: Archwardens, detachment from Fort Thornmoth
records.summary: Marshgate Watch is a road post on the coast road south of Thorn. Wardens check goods and travellers moving between Thorn, the bight villages and Arorha.

notes.text: A small garrison post where the Thorn road crosses the neck of land at the bight's northern end. The name follows the Marches' habit of naming posts for what they watch.

notes.text: Built by the Imperial Commission as a toll and way-station for the Thorn-Archon road. It stood empty from the secession until the Archwardens' detachment took it back as a customs point on the east road.

sources.title: Archwardens hold the Imperial '-moth' forts and run customs at the road; Skeith smugglers (state 10.2)

notes.text: Six wardens rotate through from Fort Thornmoth. They take the customs toll on clay and salt and watch the shore for boats that avoid Thorn.

sources.title: Archwardens hold the Imperial '-moth' forts and run customs at the road; Skeith smugglers (state 10.2)

notes.text: Six Argonian wardens of old Archein lines, in patched half-Imperial livery, led by a sergeant who owns the post's one cutlass.

Giant snakes, swamp-crocodiles in the ditch and smugglers landing by night who fight when asked to pay.
A warden has been letting Skeith smugglers' boats through for pay. The sergeant wants the man caught before the blame falls on the sergeant.

records.name: Zeeraxun Roost
records.held_by: The Sarpa of the Zeeraxun roost
records.summary: Zeeraxun Roost is a camp of the winged Sarpa on a rise in the marsh behind Hatandros Bight. They keep apart, drive off outsiders and stay near the Virtluush ruin.

notes.text: A permanent camp of Sarpa, one of the winged interior breeds, on high ground behind the bight. A roost this far east is a long way from the Sarpa's home in the middle of the province.

notes.text: A camp of tents and perches, with scouts on the high perches at dawn. The Sarpa watch the road to Arorha and drive off clay-diggers who come near.

notes.text: About nine Sarpa, led by an old female who speaks Jel and a few words of Dunmeri. They are cautiously willing to trade for dye and salt if a visitor approaches openly.

notes.text: Feathers, bird-eggs and fish; they trade for salt and clay beads at the edge of their ground. Ash-glass picked from Virtluush is their one valuable good.
The Sarpa hold the wind to be a messenger of the Hist and read omens in flight patterns. They keep a rack of old Velothi ancestor-bones on a post as a boundary mark.
Tents of woven reed and hide on a rise, tall poles with feathered streamers, nets slung between trees, droppings white on the stones.
Sarpa archers shoot intruders from the perches; the camp's boundary poles are marked in feathers and bones.

records.held_by: No one; ancestor ghosts and Sarpa scouts
records.summary: Virtluush is a ruined Cantemiric Velothi settlement inland of Hatandros Bight, once a river-fort. A Sarpa roost sits beside it.

notes.text: A bigger Velothi ruin on a river bend behind the bight, with a Sarpa camp at its flank. It is one of the Cantemiric Velothi settlements of this seaboard.
Cantemiric Velothi held it until the Knahaten Flu (2E 560-603) ended them. It stood on a river bend with a boat road to the coast.

sources.title: Velothi holds died in the Flu 2E 560-603; Dunmer relic-buyers at Thorn; Sarpa roost beside it (state 10.1, 10.3)

notes.text: Collapsed courts, a standing tower and a deep cistern, haunted. The Sarpa live beside it and take ash-glass and tablets from the edges but will not go into the lower halls.

notes.text: Once a river-fort that took tolls from boat traffic. Now a scavenger's draw: Velothi bronze, ash-glass, ancestor tablets and a locked vault of dye-stuffs.

notes.text: Mephala-influenced Velothi ancestor worship: altar niches to a Daedric lord and carved family tablets in every room.
Black stone courts and a tall broken tower in heavy Velothi courses, ivy and vines over the walls, a cistern with dark water in the heart.
Ancestor ghosts, skeletal guards and a Sarpa lookout who will shoot anyone who approaches by air or reed-path.

records.summary: Ysan is a small coastal landing of Tsonac's stone-building people on Hatandros Bight. Quarried stone and timber come down here by river to be shipped to Thorn.

notes.text: A hamlet at the bight's northern shore where the stone and timber of the Tsonac-Kaleel reach the sea. Its culture is that of Tsonac.
Founded as a coast landing by Tsonac in the settled generations after 4E 48, when Thorn's builders began buying stone again. The freight path down from the jungle uplands is older than the hamlet.

notes.text: A hamlet of Helstrom's people, set on the open coast far from any Hist tree. The Root-Folk's hunting and egg-tending stations spread through the inner swamp. This is their outlier on the sea.
Founded in the generations after 4E 48, to keep watch on the sea; its people came from the Lake Ulaish country by canoe.

records.name: Aroxhu
records.held_by: The council of village elders of the Oxhu-Teeleel, meeting under the Aroxhu Hist
records.summary: Aroxhu is the great mound-town of the Clay-Mound People, the largest tribal settlement of the east interior. Its council of elders speaks for the whole confederacy and meets under its Hist.

notes.text: The seat of the Oxhu-Teeleel confederacy, a mound-town of red clay with a Hist at its centre, nearly forty people, a small city by the standard of the interior. The confederacy was made from many interior tribes whose names outsiders do not know.

sources.title: The interior tribes were never emptied and rule everything outside the cities through tree-minders and a Hist (state §10.2); the Aroxhu clay-mound confederacy holds Okuwun-Rahei (state §10.2 holdings); the Archwardens hold only tolls and customs, so they must bargain (state §10.2)

notes.text: Raised over generations on a clay ridge above the low ground; it never held a stone wall. The Arorha and Inoja families moved up to its mounds when raiders burned their lowland villages, and it became the confederacy's centre.

notes.text: A busy mound-town: the council meets each new moon under the Hist, the potters' kilns burn day and night and the Archwardens must bargain for any road or toll in Oxhu country.
